goal: Build a small React app this weekend, something like a habit tracker with local storage
interpretation: By the end of the weekend, the learner has built and run a working habit tracker in React (Vite) that persists data to localStorage, and understands the hooks and component patterns behind it.
assumptions: Habit tracker means: add/delete habits, mark them complete per day, view streaks, with data persisted in localStorage
The 360 minutes is pure watching time, so a long project build video can serve as the backbone
Plain JavaScript (not TypeScript) is fine since the learner knows JS fundamentals but did not mention TypeScript
Modern function components and hooks only; class components are not needed
The 'nothing before 2022' constraint is handled by the later video-selection step using upload dates; the exclusions here cover title-based filters only

sub_topics.title: Vite project setup and React project structure
sub_topics.why: The learner knows npm but not Vite; they need to scaffold a modern React project and understand the folder layout, dev server and build, instead of using create-react-app.

sub_topics.title: JSX and function components with props
sub_topics.why: As a JS-literate backend dev, they need the mental model of JSX as JS expressions plus component composition and props to build UI.

sub_topics.title: State with useState and event handling
sub_topics.why: A habit tracker is driven by state (habits list, completion toggles); they need immutable updates of arrays/objects and form handling.

sub_topics.title: useEffect and persisting state to localStorage
sub_topics.why: Persistence is a core requirement; they need to understand effects, dependency arrays, lazy state initialization and JSON serialization (which they already know).

sub_topics.title: Component patterns: lifting state up, lists and keys, custom hooks
sub_topics.why: To structure a multi-component app cleanly, they need to share state between components, render lists correctly, and extract a reusable useLocalStorage hook.

sub_topics.title: Build a habit tracker / similar small app end-to-end
sub_topics.why: Following a project build ties all concepts together and mirrors the weekend goal; it is the backbone of the plan.

sub_topics.title: Streak logic, styling and finishing touches
sub_topics.why: The learner needs to adapt the tutorial project into their own habit tracker by adding date-based completion and streak calculation.

picks.title: Build a Complete To-Do List App with React + Vite | Dashboard, Reminders & Local Storage Tutorial
picks.reason: A short, project-based React + Vite build with no red flags. Per its summary and segment map it goes from Vite setup through JSX components, useState and event handling to useEffect + localStorage, and it also covers lists/keys. That gives a Python engineer a fast first pass through the whole stack on a small app.
picks.confidence_note: Card has no verified quotes, and its 27-minute duration conflicts with segment timestamps running to 45:00. Higher if the full build is confirmed; lower if the later segments are missing.

picks.title: Build a Todo App with React.js | Beginner React Project using hooks
picks.reason: A full hour-long build of a hooks-based todo app (useState, useEffect, localStorage, CSS animations) that is almost the same shape as a habit tracker (add/delete/toggle items, persisted). It is the project backbone, and you can adapt its list and toggle logic to habits and days. The card is unflagged and project-based.
picks.confidence_note: The card has no segment breakdown or verified quotes. It uploaded in Nov 2022, so Vite usage is uncertain (vite_setup relevance is 1), which is why X92 comes first for setup.

picks.title: ReactJS Tutorial 81: Creating Our Own useLocalStorage Hook In ReactJS
picks.reason: Builds a custom useLocalStorage hook that combines useState and useEffect. This is the custom-hook pattern the learner needs and the two project builds don't clearly teach. Use it to refactor the habit tracker's persistence into a reusable hook.
picks.confidence_note: It is flagged pure_theory and is a short concept explainer. I picked it only because no unflagged candidate clearly covers custom hooks. The card shows no verified quotes and its segment map covers only the first 8 of 16 minutes.

warnings: Budget use is about 105 of 360 minutes (29%). About 255 minutes are unused because the remaining candidates were flagged, unverifiable (poor transcripts), pre-2022, off-stack (Redux/Next.js/TypeScript) or redundant. I chose to under-fill rather than pad with weak videos.
None of the cards had verified quotes, so evidence_quote_ids are empty and all confidence values are moderate. The picks rest on summaries, topics and segment maps only.

No candidate teaches habit-specific streak logic or per-day completion tracking. You will need to write the streak calculation yourself, using the todo builds' list and toggle patterns plus plain JavaScript date handling.

Component patterns are only partly covered. Lists/keys and composition come from the build videos, and custom hooks from the short hook video. Lifting state up is covered only implicitly in the builds, and no video teaches it explicitly.
Both builds are plain JavaScript todo apps rather than habit trackers. The QdT video is from 2022 and may not use Vite, so rely on the X92 video for Vite setup.
The X92 card lists 27 minutes of runtime but segment timestamps up to 45:00. I counted 27 minutes toward the budget.
The 'at most two videos per creator' constraint is satisfied: all three picks come from different creators.
